Then, I reminded myself why not sign up for 6 months and see how it goes for me. Maybe, I will eventually learn boxing skills while losing some weight right? So I did.

I also couldn't forget how I stayed back with the rest of the members to surprise Coach Kumar on his birthday! The members brought food that we could eat as we chitchatted and decorated the gym to feel the birthday spirit. It makes me feel like a family! The bond, the joy and the rapport were present.
Of course, I will not forget the lovely ladies, Ms. Grace and Ms. Sharifah who have been so patient in answering questions and concerns! They always have a big smile on their faces every time I enter the gym!
KOS is not just a gym! It is my new family. To the coaches, coach Faz, coach Krishna, coach Kumar and coach Jo... Thank you for motivating me and always telling me that I can do it! Surprisingly, the harder the training gets, the more I'm loving it. Every workout challenges me physically and mentally, and seeing my progress over time has been incredibly rewarding.

One of my favourite parts of MT30 is the boxing workouts. It's a fantastic way to relieve stress and clear your mind after a long day. I love hitting the bags, working up a sweat, and walking out feeling accomplished and refreshed.

What really stands out is their 6-Week Challenge. The team doesn't just focus on exercise; they also help you understand your nutrition and lifestyle habits. They calculate your calorie needs, provide useful recommendations, and offer guidance that is realistic and easy to follow.

Having that level of support has made it much easier to stay accountable and achieve my goals.

Another big plus is their schedule, the last class starts at 8:45 PM, which is perfect for those who work late. There's no need to rush after work, and it makes staying consistent with training much easier.

A special shout-out to Ben for being part of my fitness journey since day one. Thank you for the constant encouragement, motivation, and support.

Having someone who genuinely believes in your progress makes a huge difference, and I truly appreciate all the guidance along the way.

The biggest difference is the coaching style. Our previous gym was very disciplinary in approach, which over time became demoralising for both my son and me. I want to be fair here and say that some people genuinely thrive under that kind of strict coaching, and I respect that. It just wasn’t right for us. At Spartans Springleaf, Coaches Zak (Head Coach), Danish, and Khlifi have made boxing enjoyable again. For the first time in a long while, my son and I are actually looking forward to training. And the fun comes with real credibility — these are highly qualified coaches and ex-national boxers, so you’re getting proper technique and genuine expertise alongside all the encouragement.

A special mention has to go to Head Coach Zak. His patience really stands out, and even on a bad training day he never makes you feel lousy or judged. On top of that, he has a real gift for bringing out the fun in boxing. That combination is exactly what my son and I needed, and it’s a big part of why we look forward to every session. The rest of the coaches are fantastic too.

The facilities are also a clear step up. Spartans Springleaf is more updated, air-conditioned, and you can tell they put real effort into hygiene. Our old gym was naturally ventilated, but the upkeep didn’t keep pace - spoilt fans weren’t repaired or replaced promptly, and the sponge flooring stayed tattered and torn for the entire 1.5 years we were there without ever being replaced.

One note for anyone comparing gyms in the north by their ratings: review count doesn’t tell the whole story. Our previous gym actively asked members to leave Google reviews, whereas Spartans Springleaf simply lets the coaching speak for itself. They may have fewer reviews than others nearby, but in our experience they’re the better gym by a clear margin.

Throughout the years, Master Chan always made double sure to check on me, and would remind the instructor taking me that I have asthma and to be double careful. Immediately, I pledged my loyalty to RTF and Master Chan and signed a package.

What I really like that spurs my almost compulsive decision?

1.  The price is really affordable. I was doing Muay Thai at a franchise gym, and it costs me $70/session on top of the monthly membership fee of $145. So when Master Chan offered me the package I couldn't refuse.

2. The First In - First Out training style. You reach, you skip, you HIIT, and then padworks with the trainers. Not your turn yet? Go practise moves on those sandbags. I've never tried other gyms so I can't compare training style but this style works for me.

3. The camaraderie among the students. Students who goes there really just wants to have fun and keep fit at the same time. There's no competition and each of us genuinely wants to help each other improve. Some students are now trainers as well. You progress at your own speed.

4. The open air gym. It's so old school, I like. Open air training is better for muay thai. You don't really want your sweats to get chilled by aircon. Oh, they have ceiling fans but it's not operational during training. Warnings given in advance.

The Khan levels was introduced a few years after I joined them. They'll prep you before the exams so you'll know what to expect. And when you reach Khan 3 and 4, you will be able to join the muay thai competition to fight with the students in Thailand's affiliated gym, or the International Muay Thai Festival fights with other overseas competitors. tldr gave my budget 💲and they said it fit my budget but realised after my trial that it didnt 🥹, messy handling of communication 📱😥 and got blamed when giving feedback about precautions ⚠️😓

1. Informed them about my budget and checked if they had plans that fit. They had 0 disclosure about the price scheme so I was sure they had both monthly pricing and lesson packages like I've seen when checking with other martial arts centres.

However, to my shock, they informed me they only had monthly classes and surprise! It did not fit my budget, it would be great if I was informed of this earlier. But I was asked to pay 30 and go for the trial just to know about the cost. I admit I took the risk even though I didn't know what type of pricing they had, and I guess it was my fault trusting that they could fit my budget 😅

Tried to talk over whatsapp about it but the lack of sympathy is quite astonishing to be honest 😅

2. Was told that I would be introduced to the prices after the trial and if I didn't sign up on the spot, there would be no waiver. However, I checked with the trainer after the trial that day and she told me I would be contacted through whatsapp. My trial ended at 12pm, and I waited till 3.30pm without any message from them before I contacted them myself. After which I was left there for about 4 hours before I was introduced to the price at night when I was already asleep.

I understand they may be busy, but telling me there was only waiver if I signed up on the spot/ on the day itself and then taking so long to reply really gave me a lot of anxiety. I felt like my time wasn't appreciated at all and I was chasing them for a reply. Didn't sign up after this harrowing experience, so I didn't know if they would've given me the waiver anyway despite what they said.

3. I had rings on my right hand before starting the class and pardon my folly and lack of basic knowledge, but I wasn't aware that it was very important to remove all the jewelry before wearing the boxing gloves. Sometimes people may forget to remove them too, even if it is basic knowledge. The instructor didn't inform me of any precautions and there were no signages in the space, so I didn't remove my rings. During the session, I asked if it was normal if my fingers hurt while punching and the trainer said it might have been because I didn't have my gloves on. Removed my gloves at the end of the class, saw my ring, and realised it might have been the problem. A short search online made me realise it posed a risk for significant injury!

I gave some feedback over whatsapp because I hoped more precautions would be taken so others wouldn't be at risk of injury, but lo and behold, I was blamed for it 😅😅

Thanks for reading this lengthy review and I really hope the owner takes these feedback into account. To be honest, I liked that this was a women's only gym and the class was pretty enjoyable, but my experience communicating over Whatsapp has ruined my impression of this muay thai centre. My experience is stated factually and I did not have the goal of bashing this business. [{"Name":"Jacque Fernandez","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjUkfK3TI0Dv6Jxk6PgI9teayrwFHP-u1Z3zjyRIl-wkj8ozMIFy=s120-c-rp-mo-br100","Rating":1,"Description":"I was a member in Neuefit for the past 2 years for BJJ, joined and stayed because of the coaches and community.

I genuinely appreciate the effort that Prof Amirul & Coach Daryl put into helping members improve. Unfortunately, my overall experience deteriorated over time due to several recurring issues.

One of the biggest frustrations was the frequent class cancellations, often with very short notice or at times little to no notice at all. Cancellations felt normalised with no replacement coaches at times and as a paying member, it became difficult to plan training consistently when classes could be cancelled at the last minute. Most of us felt shortchanged.

Another concern was the cleanliness and maintenance of the facility. Hygiene standards were not always up to expectations and there were occasions where cockroaches were spotted within the gym premises. This was concerning, especially in a martial arts gym utilising the mats 100% of the time for a high contact sport like jiu jitsu.

What disappointed me most was that these were not isolated incidents. The issues persisted over an extended period and despite feedback from members, there appeared to be little meaningful effort to address or improve them over the past months. As a result, I have since decided to terminate my membership and unfortunately the coaches and community I stayed for have also decided to move on to other opportunities.

Neuefit had strong community and coaches at that time and I’m grateful for the experiences, time spent and friends made but management, operational reliability, communication and facility upkeep need significant improvement.

Providing a clean, professional and dependable training environment should always be priority.

Unfortunately, the move to Raffles Place at the beginning of 2026 marked a significant decline in the overall experience.

The previous Kallang Wave Mall facility was outstanding; great vibes, spacious, better equipped, and offered a far more comfortable training environment. The new space is now half the size, depressing and dirty.

Small gym
- Chaotic and overstimulating atmosphere with Muay Thai, HIIT and BJJ classes all running concurrently in a small space
- Limited space to roll safely without the risk of bumping into people, stairs, or the reception counter

Feedback was often met with excuses or promises that never seemed to materialize
- Changing rooms: As a female member, this was my main concern. I’ve raised that the changing areas were separated only by curtains, that they could be easily blown open by the air-conditioning, and that anyone could pull them open without knowing there’s someone inside. Many members also suggested replacing them with proper doors to provide privacy and security. This was raised in January,  and curtains were changed to doors only in June, after many members had already become frustrated. It is quite telling when members feel more comfortable changing and using mall’s toilets before coming to the gym.

Hygiene standards were an ongoing issue
- The shower areas frequently smelled of pee
- Cockroaches seen at changing area, water cooler area, mats) on several occasions
- After classes, our white gis would often turn grey. (We were told that a deep clean would be carried out, but this never happened)

Communication between management and members was often poor. Operational staff were not particularly effective in their roles
- Last minute class cancellations
- Important changes, such as the departure of key coaches and the gym’s relocation, were often communicated very late, and we usually hear about such information via word of mouth from other members instead of from the gym directly
- Members had to personally ask staff to verify our membership validity periods, as they were incorrect due to gym relocation extensions or injury breaks etc. These were never updated proactively for the rest of the members though several of us has already asked them to. Hence, to date, members who have never realised / asked would still have been shortchanged

Sadly, there used to be a fantastic community and a strong team of coaches that made the place special. Members genuinely wanted to see the gym flourish, do well, and grow its community. We’ve tried giving feedback and gave them time to make changes, yet things still remained unchanged. Eventually, people simply gave up. Now that the best coaches and many of the long-time members have left, I have unfortunately decided to leave as well.

I hope, moving forward, the management will be more receptive to member’s feedback, rather than assuming overall satisfaction with their current efforts, when that is not reflected in members’ private conversations at all.

I later heard across the window that the comment had been joked about among themselves, which made it even more inappropriate. One of the other people in the gym even questioned her about what she had said to me, to which she responded proudly, “What? It's true what.”

Barely three minutes into the class, Coach Choco came out and told me, “She can’t skip leh, Not suitable for her.” My daughter is only 4 years old and was genuinely trying her best to learn how to skip using an adult-sized skipping rope.

So no room at all for improvement?

Halfway through the class, my daughter needed to use the washroom. When she returned, there was little to no encouragement or guidance given to her. She eventually became upset, broke down and left the class.

Again, no room at all for improvement.
